name: Spaghetti aglio e olio
steps: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti 1 minute less than the package says; save 1 cup of the pasta water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, put the olive oil and garlic in a large cold pan and heat over medium-low for 3–4 minutes, until the garlic is pale golden (don't let it brown or it turns bitter).
Stir in the red pepper flakes, then add the drained spaghetti and 1/2 cup of the pasta water.
Toss over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until the sauce clings and looks glossy, adding a splash more water if dry.
Season with salt, then top with parsley and parmesan if using.

name: Penne with tomato sauce
steps: Heat the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat, add the garlic, and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, add the italian seasoning, a pinch of sugar if the tomatoes taste sour, and 1/2 tsp salt; simmer on low for 15–20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Meanwhile, cook the penne in a large pot of salted boiling water according to the package; drain.
Toss the penne with the sauce and serve topped with parmesan and torn basil if you have it.

name: Spaghetti bolognese
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat; add the onion and carrot and cook 6–8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the ground beef, and cook 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned with no pink left and it reaches 160°F.
Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the crushed tomatoes and 1 tsp salt. Simmer uncovered on low for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick.
Near the end, cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water according to the package; drain.
Toss the spaghetti with the sauce and serve with parmesan.

name: Baked ziti
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the pasta in salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the package says, then drain.
In the empty pot, stir the marinara, italian seasoning, and cream cheese (if using) over low heat until smooth, then mix in the pasta and half the mozzarella.
Spread in a 9x13-inch baking dish and top with the remaining mozzarella and the parmesan.
Bake uncovered 20–25 minutes until bubbling and the cheese is melted and golden in spots. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Creamy garlic chicken pasta
steps: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water according to the package; save 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken 6–8 minutes, stirring, until golden and cooked through to 165°F; move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, melt the butter, and cook the garlic 1 minute. Pour in the cream and simmer gently 3 minutes.
Stir in the parmesan until melted, then add the spinach (if using) until wilted.
Return the chicken, add the pasta, and toss, loosening with pasta water as needed. Season to taste and serve.

name: Pasta primavera
steps: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water; add the broccoli for the last 3 minutes. Save 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain together.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and cook the zucchini and bell pepper 5–6 minutes until tender-crisp.
Add the garlic and cherry tomatoes and cook 2 minutes until the tomatoes just soften.
Add the pasta and broccoli, the lemon juice, the parmesan, and a splash of pasta water; toss over low heat 1 minute, season with salt, and serve.

name: Pasta e ceci (chickpea pasta soup)

ingredients.note: small shapes like ditalini or broken spaghetti
use vegetable broth to keep it vegetarian

steps: Heat the olive oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion 5 minutes until soft; add the garlic and a pinch of red pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the chickpeas and vegetable broth and bring to a boil.
Scoop out about 1 cup of the chickpeas, mash them with a fork, and stir them back in to thicken the soup.
Add the pasta and simmer over medium-low 10–12 minutes, stirring often, until tender; add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Season with salt and serve with parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Lemon garlic shrimp pasta

ingredients.note: peeled and deveined, thawed if frozen

steps: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water according to the package; save 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
Pat the shrimp dry and season with salt. Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp 1–2 minutes per side until pink and opaque; move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the butter, garlic, and red pepper flakes, and cook 1 minute.
Add the lemon zest, lemon juice, pasta, and a splash of pasta water; toss until glossy.
Return the shrimp, toss to warm through, and serve topped with parsley.

name: Sausage and peppers
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and brown the sausage links 8–10 minutes, turning, then move to a plate and slice into thick coins.
In the same pan, cook the bell pepper strips and onion with a pinch of salt for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until soft and lightly browned.
Add the garlic and italian seasoning and cook 1 minute.
Return the sausage, cover, and cook on medium-low 5–6 minutes until the sausage reaches 160°F inside. Serve as is or piled into the rolls (bread).

name: Chicken parmesan

ingredients.note: large, sliced in half horizontally into 4 cutlets

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Season the chicken cutlets with salt. Beat the egg in a shallow bowl; mix the breadcrumbs with half the parmesan in another.
Dip each cutlet in egg, then press into the breadcrumb mix to coat.
Heat the oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat and fry the cutlets 2–3 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Spoon the marinara over the chicken and top with the mozzarella and remaining parmesan.
Bake 10–12 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and the chicken reaches 165°F inside. Serve with pasta or salad.

name: Caprese salad
steps: Arrange the tomato and mozzarella slices on a plate, overlapping and alternating.
Tuck basil leaves between the slices.
Drizzle with the olive oil and a little vinegar if using, then sprinkle with salt and pepper and serve right away.

name: Bruschetta

ingredients.note: baguette or crusty bread, 1/2 inch thick

steps: Mix the tomatoes, minced garlic, basil, 2 tbsp olive oil, vinegar if using, and 1/2 tsp salt in a bowl; let sit 5 minutes.
Brush the bread slices with the remaining oil and toast under the broiler on high (or in a toaster) 1–2 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Rub the warm toast with the cut side of the halved garlic clove.
Spoon the tomato mixture onto the toast just before serving so it stays crisp.

name: Minestrone

ingredients.note: use vegetable broth to keep it vegetarian

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, carrots, and celery 8 minutes until softened.
Add the zucchini and italian seasoning and cook 2 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, and chickpeas; bring to a boil, then simmer on low 15 minutes.
Stir in the pasta and simmer 10 minutes more until tender. Season with salt and serve, with parmesan on top if you like.

name: Tuscan chickpea and spinach stew

ingredients.note: use vegetable broth to keep it vegetarian

steps: Heat the olive oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion 5 minutes until soft; add the garlic and italian seasoning for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas, diced tomatoes, and vegetable broth; simmer on medium-low 15 minutes, lightly mashing a few chickpeas to thicken.
Stir in the spinach a handful at a time until wilted, about 2 minutes. Season with salt.
Serve topped with parmesan, with crusty bread for dipping.

name: Mushroom risotto

ingredients.note: arborio is best; regular long-grain white rice works too, just a little less creamy
kept warm; use vegetable broth to keep it vegetarian

steps: Warm the vegetable broth in a small pot on low. Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and cook the mushrooms 6–7 minutes until browned; move to a bowl.
Lower to medium, add 1 tbsp butter and the onion, and cook 4 minutes until soft; add the garlic for 30 seconds.

Add the rice (arborio, or regular white rice is fine) and stir 1 minute to coat. Add the warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting until each is mostly absorbed, for 18–22 minutes, until the rice is tender with a slight bite.
Stir in the mushrooms, the remaining butter, and the parmesan; season with salt. It should be loose and creamy — add a splash more broth if it's stiff.

name: Chicken piccata

ingredients.note: large, sliced in half horizontally into 4 thin cutlets

steps: Season the chicken cutlets with salt and pepper, then dredge in the flour and shake off the extra.
Heat the olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 3–4 minutes per side until golden and it reaches 165°F; move to a plate.
Lower to medium, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then pour in the broth and lemon juice, scraping up the browned bits. Simmer 3–4 minutes until reduced by about half.
Turn off the heat, swirl in the remaining butter, return the chicken to coat it in the sauce, and top with parsley.

name: Greek salad
steps: Put the tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and bell pepper in a large bowl.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, half the oregano, and a pinch of salt, then pour over the vegetables and toss.
Top with the feta, sprinkle with the remaining oregano, and serve.

name: Chicken souvlaki pitas
steps: Toss the chicken with the lemon juice, 2 tbsp olive oil, two-thirds of the garlic, the oregano, and 1 tsp salt; marinate 15 minutes (or up to 8 hours in the fridge).
Make tzatziki: mix the yogurt, grated cucumber, remaining garlic, and a pinch of salt.
Heat the remaining oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken 8–10 minutes, turning, until golden and it reaches 165°F.
Fill each warm pita with chicken, tzatziki, tomato, and red onion.

name: Baked chickpea patties
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Mash the chickpeas well with a fork or potato masher, then mix in the breadcrumbs, egg, garlic, cumin, herbs, and 1/2 tsp salt.
Shape into 8 small patties about 1/2 inch thick, place on the sheet, and brush the tops with olive oil.
Bake 20–25 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and firm. Serve in pita or with yogurt for dipping.

name: Hummus

ingredients.note: or carrot and cucumber sticks, for dipping

steps: Put the chickpeas, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, olive oil, and 1/2 tsp salt in a blender or food processor. (This is a simple tahini-free version; add 3 tbsp tahini if you have it.)
Blend 2–3 minutes, adding 2–4 tbsp of the saved chickpea liquid or cold water, until very smooth.
Taste and adjust salt and lemon, then spread in a bowl, drizzle with olive oil, and dust with paprika. Serve with pita.

name: Lemon herb chicken thighs
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Pat the chicken thighs dry.
Mix the olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, garlic, italian seasoning, 1 tsp salt, and some pepper; rub all over the chicken.
Place skin-side up in a baking dish or on a sheet pan and roast 35–40 minutes until the skin is golden and crisp and the thickest part reaches 165°F.
Rest 5 minutes, then spoon the pan juices over the top to serve.

name: Greek lemon potatoes

ingredients.note: use vegetable broth to keep it vegetarian

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
In a 9x13-inch baking dish, toss the potatoes with the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, 1 tsp salt, and pepper, then pour the vegetable broth around them.
Roast 25 minutes, flip the potatoes, and roast 20–25 minutes more until the liquid is mostly absorbed and the edges are golden and crisp.
Taste, add a squeeze more lemon or salt if needed, and serve.

name: Tuna pasta salad

ingredients.note: short shapes like fusilli or penne

steps: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water according to the package, drain, and rinse under cold water until cool.
Whisk the lemon juice and olive oil with 1/2 tsp salt and some pepper in a large bowl.
Add the pasta, tuna (broken into flakes), cherry tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and herbs; toss well.
Serve right away or chill up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Pita pizzas
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Place the pitas on a baking sheet and brush lightly with olive oil.
Spread each pita with marinara, leaving a small border, then top with mozzarella, bell pepper, and mushrooms.
Sprinkle with italian seasoning and bake 8–10 minutes until the cheese is melted and the edges are crisp.

name: Zucchini parmesan bake
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Toss the zucchini rounds with 1 tbsp olive oil, the italian seasoning, and a pinch of salt.
Spread a thin layer of marinara in an 8x8-inch baking dish, then layer half the zucchini, half the remaining sauce, and half the mozzarella; repeat.
Mix the parmesan, breadcrumbs, and remaining oil and scatter over the top.
Bake 25–30 minutes until bubbling, the zucchini is tender, and the top is golden. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Lentil soup

ingredients.note: use vegetable broth to keep it vegetarian

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, carrots, and celery 8 minutes until soft; add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, diced tomatoes, and vegetable broth; bring to a boil.
Reduce to low, cover partly, and simmer 25–30 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Stir in the lemon juice and season with salt. For a thicker soup, mash some of the lentils against the side of the pot.

name: Baked salmon with lemon and herbs

ingredients.note: if you have no fresh herbs

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with foil or parchment.
Place the salmon skin-side down and season with salt and pepper. Mix the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, and herbs (or italian seasoning) and spoon over the fillets; top with lemon slices.
Bake 12–15 minutes until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily with a fork (145°F in the thickest part).
Serve with the pan juices spooned over.

name: Cacio e pepe
steps: Cook the spaghetti in a pot of lightly salted boiling water (use less water than usual so it gets starchy) until just al dente; save 1 1/2 cups pasta water, then drain.
In a large pan over medium heat, toast the black pepper 1 minute until fragrant, then add the butter and 1/2 cup pasta water and let it bubble.

Turn the heat to low, add the spaghetti, and toss. Take the pan off the heat and add the parmesan a handful at a time, tossing constantly and adding splashes of pasta water, until a smooth, creamy sauce forms.
Serve right away with extra pepper and cheese on top.
